RESTATEMENT -- March 2026 Revenue (EPISODE B, financial reporting error)

Monthly/Archive/2026-03/monthly.xlsx was NEVER updated after a 2026-07-22 correction and still shows STALE, UNDERSTATED March 2026 Revenue: $13,111,960.23. The AUTHORITATIVE March 2026 Revenue is $13,729,801.29, taken from consolidated-revised.xlsx ('Revised Authoritative March-June Package', tab 'Income Statement', March row) -- confirmed by direct read on this build date. This model's March 2026 Revenue cell is sourced from consolidated-revised.xlsx, NOT Archive/2026-03/monthly.xlsx. Reported EBITDA for March 2026 is UNCHANGED at $2,618,535.91 in both the stale Archive file and consolidated-revised.xlsx -- the restatement was a pure Revenue/Cost gross-up ($617,841.06 on each side), EBITDA-neutral (independently verified: Revenue - Costs - OpEx ties to 2,618,535.91 under both the original and corrected figures per consolidated-revised.xlsx's own Costs/Operating Expenses columns, which do not exist in the standard monthly Archive schema). April, May and June 2026 are NOT restated -- verified identical between consolidated-revised.xlsx and their respective Archive/June-package files (Revenue and Reported EBITDA match to the penny for all three months). Old->new logged in restatements.json: Mar 2026 Revenue $13,111,960.23 -> $13,729,801.29 (material: diff $617,841.06, 4.71% of the old value, well above the $25k/1% threshold).

Full scan performed across all 22 months: each Archive month's own package compared against consolidated-revised.xlsx (the only file whose range overlaps any Archive month, covering Mar-Jun 2026) and against June_2026_Monthly_Package.xlsx for June. Result: only March 2026 Revenue differs (see above); April/May/June match exactly; no other month has a second source to compare against (each Archive month is a single-period snapshot with no other overlapping file). No prior canonical model existed for this borrower (first build) so no prior-snapshot diff applies.
Income Statement -- thin monthly cadence (JUDGMENT CALL, per borrower-config.json model_lines._gap_note)

The borrower's monthly Income Statement has ONLY three rows -- Revenue, Reported EBITDA, EBITDA margin -- with NO Gross Profit, COGS, Net Income, or D&A anywhere in the monthly cadence (not on the IS, not on the Cash Flow tab). model_lines.gross_profit / operating_cogs / net_income / depreciation_amortization are left BLANK/unmapped rather than derived or guessed -- three-statement-analysis will report them in lines_not_found with dependent ratios suppressed. opex_groups is intentionally EMPTY (no opex line at all exists). Both 'Revenue' and 'Reported EBITDA' are entered as hardcoded (blue) source lines -- there is no intermediate detail within this sheet to build EBITDA up from, so Reported EBITDA is NOT a computed subtotal here (unlike Asteron/Nemeris, where component cost lines exist).

Per covenant-spec.json#/definitions/EBITDA, compute.ebitda_bridge = 'Reported EBITDA' -- the model's own single pinned EBITDA row, bound directly with NO addback. Verified at three independent points that 'Reported EBITDA' ties EXACTLY to the certified 'Covenant EBITDA': Mar 2026 both 2,618,535.91; Jun 2026 both 2,696,995.08; May 2026 both 2,588,973.90. This EBITDA bridge is NOT provisional -- it is the covenant-spec-directed definition, with a covenant-spec.json present.

model_lines.interest_expense maps to the Cash Flow tab's 'Cash interest' line; model_lines.taxes maps to 'Cash taxes' -- both cash-basis, not accrual IS rows (there is no accrual IS interest/tax line at all in this borrower's monthly cadence).
Balance Sheet -- NO native Balance Sheet exists (JUDGMENT CALL, per borrower-config.json analysis_lines._omitted_note)

This borrower's monthly package carries NO Balance Sheet tab at all -- only a 'Working Capital' tab (Accounts receivable, Accounts payable, Net working capital) and a 'Cash Flow' tab. The 'Balance Sheet' sheet in this model therefore carries Working Capital detail ONLY (rows 7-9): there is no Total Assets/Total Liabilities/Total Equity, and consequently NO Balance-Check row -- inventing one from non-existent data would misstate the model. This is a disclosed, borrower-config-documented gap, not an omission. Supplementary detail below the Working Capital rows (rows 11-20) reproduces the borrower's own Debt Roll-Forward tab and the covenant-support rows -- see below. 'cash' (analysis_lines.cash) maps instead to the Cash Flow Statement sheet's 'Ending cash' row, the closest thing to a period-end cash balance this borrower reports. 'inventory' is also omitted (not part of pledged collateral per collateral-map.json, and no monthly row exists to track it against, even though FY2024 annual statements show a real $8,640,818.48 inventory balance -- annual-only, not part of the monthly cadence).

Reproduces the borrower's own 'Debt Roll-Forward' tab (Beginning debt, Required principal, Draws, PIK, Ending debt) as supplementary detail below the Working Capital rows -- verified to chain exactly across all 22 months (each month's Ending debt = next month's Beginning debt, zero exceptions) and to reflect the First Amendment's amortization step-up exactly: Required principal 0.20%/month of beginning funded debt through Sep 2025 (e.g. Sep 2024: $247,603.47 = 0.20% x $123,801,733.88), stepping up to 2.00%/month from the Oct 2025 payment forward (e.g. Oct 2025: $2,412,424.66 = 2.00% x $120,621,233.10) -- a 10x step-up, confirmed. Draws and PIK are 0 in every month (single up-front-funded term loan, no delayed-draw capacity, consistent with covenant-spec.json's Funded_Debt note). model_lines.total_debt / analysis_lines.total_debt map to this block's 'Ending debt' row.
COVENANT-SUPPORT ROWS -- DEVIATION FROM STANDARD METHOD (per covenant-spec.json step7_signoff decision 'fixed_charges_component_source')

assembling-rules.md's Method step 5a normally directs populating the covenant-support rows ('Cash Interest Expense', 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments') from debt-service-schedule.json (the generated, per-month contractual schedule). For THIS borrower specifically, per the analyst's own step-7 sign-off recorded in covenant-spec.json, these two rows are instead populated directly from the borrower's own NATIVE Cash Flow tab lines ('Cash interest' and 'Required principal', both independently verified exact to the penny every month) -- NOT from debt-service-schedule.json. Rationale: Selvara carries no debt other than this one facility (no sweep-in risk the ledger-vs-contract distinction usually guards against), while the generated schedule is a known, documented APPROXIMATION (flat-original-principal-base amortization vs. the agreement's true declining-balance reality; a day-count mismatch the engine cannot reproduce -- see debt-service-spec.json ambiguities). Using the less-precise generated source on the covenant closest to an active breach (two consecutive FCCR breaches, expired waiver, next Test Date 2026-09-30 uncovered) is not defensible when a verified, more precise native source is directly available. Mechanically: 'Cash Interest Expense' (Balance Sheet row 19) = -('Cash Flow Statement' 'Cash interest' row), and 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments' (row 20) = -('Cash Flow Statement' 'Required principal' row) -- live cross-sheet formulas (not re-hardcoded) referencing the same native monthly figures already captured on the Cash Flow Statement sheet, sign-flipped to a positive expense/payment convention (matching the covenant-spec's Fixed_Charges formula, which sums Cash Interest Expense + Scheduled Debt Principal Payments + Lease payments). Cross-checked: 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments' ties exactly to the Debt Roll-Forward block's own 'Required principal' line every month (e.g. Jun 2026: both $2,052,401.70). debt-service-schedule.json exists (generated 2026-09-15) but was NOT used for these rows per this deviation -- see source-map.json's _debt_service_rows block.
Cash Flow -- as-reported, single blended waterfall (JUDGMENT CALL, per borrower-config.json analysis_lines._derived_cf_construction_note)

The native 'Cash Flow' tab is ONE blended waterfall (Beginning cash, Reported EBITDA, Cash taxes, Capital expenditures, Working-capital increase, Cash interest, Lease payments, Legacy debt payoff, New facility funding, Sponsor equity, Closing fees, Required principal, Ending cash) with NO native Operating/Investing/Financing split -- used AS REPORTED, rows 7-18, Ending cash (row 19) = SUM of all twelve, verified to chain exactly across all 22 months (each month's Ending cash = next month's Beginning cash, zero exceptions; the one large jump, Jan 2025 Beginning $11,902,593.34 -> Ending $18,843,648.31, is explained by that month's facility refinancing: Legacy debt payoff -$122,814,287.29 offset by New facility funding +$122,814,287.29, plus Sponsor equity +$12,000,000.00 and Closing fees -$4,000,000.00, consistent with the credit agreement's 2025-01-15 effective date).
Cash Flow -- TWO DERIVED subtotal rows

'Operating Cash Flow (derived)' (row 21) = Reported EBITDA + Cash taxes + Working-capital increase + Cash interest + Lease payments. 'Financing Cash Flow (derived)' (row 22) = Legacy debt payoff + New facility funding + Sponsor equity + Closing fees + Required principal. 'Capital expenditures' (native, row 10) is used DIRECTLY as Investing Cash Flow (analysis_lines.investing_cf = 'Capital expenditures') -- no separate derived row needed since Investing CF equals Capital expenditures exactly (no other investing line exists). VERIFIED against two independent months to the penny: May 2026 (Operating $1,303,642.75 + Investing -$282,314.79 + Financing -$2,094,287.45 = -$1,072,959.49 = Ending cash $11,304,193.71 - Beginning cash $12,377,153.20, exact) and June 2026 (Operating $734,796.12 + Investing -$293,149.50 + Financing -$2,052,401.70 = -$1,610,755.08 = Ending cash $9,693,438.63 - Beginning cash $11,304,193.71, exact) -- both reproduced live in the workbook's own memo tie-out rows 24-26 (diff = 0 every month). net_change_cash is left unmapped in analysis_lines -- fully recoverable as Operating + Investing + Financing, or equivalently Ending - Beginning cash, per the ties above.

Restatement / tie-out materiality threshold: the greater of $25,000 or 1% of the line, per assembling-rules.md standard. Triggered once this build: March 2026 Revenue ($617,841.06 / 4.71%, see restatement above).

Income-statement, Working Capital, Debt Roll-Forward, and Cash Flow figures foot / chain exactly for all 22 months (zero exceptions) -- see notes above. No Balance-Check row exists (no full Balance Sheet in this borrower's reporting -- disclosed gap, not an omission). Cash Flow Statement memo rows 24-26 and 28-29 reproduce the CF-vs-derived-components tie and the CF-vs-Income-Statement Reported EBITDA tie live, both = 0 every month.
